name: inprocess-obi-apb-pulp-i2c-fuzz
notes: One OBI CPU (Ibex) and the pinned PULP apb_i2c APB3 register target; no DMA model is declared, so the entry refuses F6 by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB)
the target window is the profile's own 4 KiB APB window at 0x40000000; the register map is the profile's six words (PRESCALER 0, CTRL 4, RX 8, STATUS 12, TX 16, CMD 20) and is not repeated here

the two single-bit pad inputs scl_pad_i and sda_pad_i are held at 1 (open-drain pull-up idle) by the declaration's fixed_inputs; the generic APB3 register template owns every non-bus input, so leaving them undeclared would be refused rather than defaulted
this pinned profile declares interrupts: [] and records interrupt_o as observe-only with no CPU IRQ binding, so F5 cannot be declared; the entry refuses it by name instead of inventing a vector
the cpu and target declare 50 MHz, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives both models
fuzz mode: f1_program_words 4 declares a four-word straight-line F1 program in the fixed trampoline slot, and the bounded handler wait is declared although no F5 flow is offered
